hook_text: Two bulbs, two cells, two ways to wire them. One way is dim and fragile, the other bright and tough.
clip_script: First the symbols: cell is a long line and a short fat line, lamp is a circle with a cross, switch is a gap, resistor a box, dot where wires join. Series: everything in one loop. Same current through each part. Cells add up, 1.5 plus 1.5 is 3. Lamps share: two lamps on 3 volts get 1.5 each, dim. One dies, all die. Parallel: side by side. Every lamp gets the full 3 volts, all bright, cells run down faster. One dies, the rest shine. Cells in parallel do not add volts; they last longer. Torches use series cells. Houses use parallel lamps.
visual_style: Whiteboard symbol chart; a series loop with two lamps dimming as a second is added; a parallel pair both bright with one removed and the other still lit; a torch and a house icon.
mood: Clear and quick, like a lab demo.
pacing: Symbols, series loop, dim, dies, parallel, bright, survives, torch and house.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a torch circuit and a two-lamp house circuit with proper symbols.
